beats.trigger: ## Iterate and Learn
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: to keep iterating as the landscape changes.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Grading its own work is another chance to be helpful: the self-report is the same kind of output as the thing reported on.
beats.got: The tool is too nice when it reviews itself, so I can't take its self-assessment at face value. That is worth knowing before anyone in HR relies on it.

beats.trigger: Where the account matches what you remember, you have two reads agreeing. Where it doesn't, yours counts.
beats.got: A simple rule for how much to trust the tool: my own judgment outranks it when we disagree. I can pass that on.

beats.trigger: Only you could catch a wrong line about you, which is why your own profile is the place to start.
beats.got: The person with the knowledge has to be the checker. That answers my 'who does this work' question, though only for my own profile so far.

beats.trigger: Nobody knows where agents are going, not Anthropic, not your board.
beats.got: An honest admission that nobody knows the future, and it's the first thing I could tell the leadership team. A slightly dramatic ending, though.

beats.trigger: Expect the generation rules to change a lot. The first pass is rarely right.
beats.got: The agent reviews and rewrites the rules file against what happened in the session. Fine, but I'd want to see the file myself.

beats.trigger: Each round sharpens the file: **compound interest on a rule file.**
beats.got: A repeated cycle (do, capture, reflect, sharpen) improves the file each time. That could become a team habit.

beats.trigger: Where the critic sees generic, your context is thin; add one sharp detail, then regenerate the site.
beats.got: I'm meant to use a second reader as a check, but 'cold critic' and 'regenerate' are jargon I'd have to sit with.

beats.trigger: Leading companies are investing in enablement programmes, champions networks and training
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Bring a live challenge and working access to Confluence and OneDrive.
beats.got: I need a real problem and access to our documents for next time. Both of those mean asking IT, and probably the DPO.

beats.trigger: Karpathy's LLM Wiki post; Lindenberg's memory-architecture piece, optional.
beats.got: Two names I don't know. I'll skip the optional one.

beats.trigger: Arrive with enough real material that the memory starts from your world, not generic output.
beats.got: Next session works on real material from my own work, which is better than a toy example.

beats.trigger: If stuck, scan your next two weeks of calendar; the biggest unresolved item is usually your challenge.
beats.got: I should pick a real people problem. Mine is probably the headcount question for the next leadership meeting.

beats.trigger: Open your runtime's connector settings and look for them.
beats.got: I'm told to connect the agent to our wiki and documents. This is exactly where the DPO and works council questions start, and the page doesn't mention them.

beats.trigger: Before it writes anything, ask it for a plan and approve or revise it first.
beats.got: I can ask the agent for its plan and approve it before it does anything. That's a control I can explain to people who are nervous.

beats.trigger: If a line is blank, name a fallback; do not fill it with a plausible answer.
beats.got: A three-line note to prepare. I like the instruction not to fill gaps with plausible answers. It echoes the earlier lesson, and it's a good habit in HR too.

beats.trigger: a useful system is a living pile of text the agent can read, maintain, and improve.
beats.got: The idea is that the agent's memory is just text files. I'll skim the gist.

beats.trigger: The output now travels with a file the agent re-reads next time.
beats.got: Work gets carried over in a file the agent reads next time, so it builds up.

take_homes: The agent fills gaps with generic guesses and goes easy on its own work. My own judgment decides what's true.
What one person learns can be saved in a rules file and reused by someone else's agent, so a skill can spread from me to the team.
Ask for a plan and approve it before the agent writes anything.

monday.move: Ask the DPO and the works council contact what they would need before employee data goes into an AI tool. Draft the headcount question for the leadership team.
monday.who: Kaisa, with the DPO and one HR partner
monday.stop_condition: If the DPO says employee data is off limits for now, I stop and use only non-personal material.
monday.blocker: The works council and DPO haven't been consulted, and the module never raised them.

misconception.why: The module never touched roles or headcount. It was about personal websites and rules files. I still think roles go first. The 'you decide, the agent drafts' framing leans slightly the other way, but I didn't see anyone's job discussed.

one_line: The exercise on catching the agent's flattering self-review was good, but the same 'stakeholders, best practices' paragraph keeps interrupting it, and the module never says what this means for people or for employee data.
